page: Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g-240s is a general-purpose virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is built on the x86_64 architecture and includes a 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 240 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

In benchmark testing, the server exhibits strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all scoring in the top tier. However, multi-threaded performance is more modest; the Geekbench multi-core score and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth is average, with read-only large block bandwidth at 70.96 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 41.27 GB/sec. Database operations and static web serving throughput also perform within the average range, processing 8.1 million Redis SET operations per second and delivering 14.81 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

The hardware profile offers a balanced resource density, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads that do not require massive parallelization but benefit from dedicated CPU allocation and fast local NVMe storage. Due to the discrepancy between its top-tier single-core performance and weaker multi-core scaling, this server is best suited for single-threaded tasks, text processing, lightweight database operations, and general-purpose web serving. It is less optimal for heavy multi-threaded software compilation or medium-to-large language model inference.
